title: From Sensor to Dashboard: The MQTT Pipeline Through Azure IoT Hub
description:
Most factory dashboards start at the wrong end: they show a temperature or an OEE number, but nobody can explain where the message came from or whether it can be trusted. This episode is for OT and IT architects, data engineers and manufacturing leaders building industrial IoT on Azure. Follow one telemetry message from a PLC through an edge gateway, MQTT and Azure IoT Hub into Event Hubs, storage, Microsoft Fabric and a dashboard people can act on.
In this episode
00:00 – A sensor signal is not yet manufacturing information05:28 – The edge layer between PLCs and the cloud10:57 – MQTT basics and why fleets change the problem21:53 – Azure IoT Hub, identity, TLS and the MQTT connection44:27 – Topics, payload contracts and time60:05 – QoS, routing, Event Hubs, storage and Fabric88:20 – OEE, ERP, MES and context models103:12 – Dashboards, alerts and edge resilience
Key takeaways
A raw sensor reading only becomes manufacturing information when the pipeline preserves its source, unit, quality state and source timestamp and links it to production context.Azure IoT Hub uses MQTT as a managed device connection with per-device identity, fixed topics, QoS 0 or 1 and routing, so it complements rather than replaces a local MQTT broker.Route telemetry by consumer need into Event Hubs, raw storage and Microsoft Fabric, design consumers to handle duplicates and late data, and keep safety-critical control local at the edge.

Episode page: the full episode with chapters, takeaways and FAQ on the MQTT pipelineAzure Event Hubs – the routed streaming path where consumer groups read alarm candidates, checkpoint and replay telemetryMicrosoft Fabric – where Eventstream, Eventhouse and lakehouse patterns turn routed IoT Hub telemetry into queryable dataPower BI – the consumption layer for role-based factory reports, not the system of record for machine stateRelated episode: IoT Hub Message Routing vs Event Grid — Why Telemetry and Events Are Not the Same Problem
